source_citation: SKY130A PDK (SkyWater Technology, pinned open_pdks commit 0c1f82326278a0871f0a1fc4bdacf94c88e78e4d); FreePDK45 (NCSU/OSU, North Carolina State University); ASAP7 PDK (Arizona State University); material properties from CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 103rd ed. and Ioffe Institute semiconductor database
license_or_access: Apache-2.0 (SKY130); free academic (FreePDK45); free academic (ASAP7); public CRC/Ioffe data

sky130a.core_soa_note: Strict 1.95 V core safe-operating-area ceiling for SKY130 core devices (li1 to met5)
sky130a.ox_breakdown_note: SiO2 intrinsic breakdown ~10 MV/cm; SKY130 practical TDDB-limited operating ceiling set by foundry spec to 1.95 V for core devices

freepdk45.note: Virtual PDK for academic research; no fabricated silicon. Published nominal VDD = 1.0 V

asap7.note: Virtual predictive PDK from ASU; no fabricated silicon. Published nominal VDD = 0.7 V

silicon.thermal_conductivity_note: at 300 K; decreases with T approximately as T^(-1.5) above 100 K

copper.fusing_note: Joule fusing depends on geometry and pulse duration — use Onderdonk or Preece equations for specific traces

aluminium.electromigration_note: SKY130 metal is Al with TiN barrier; Black's equation applies for EM lifetime

niobium.note: Type-II superconductor; used in superconducting quantum circuits

fr4_pcb.note: FR-4 standard PCB substrate; Tg ~130 °C, delamination threshold ~260 °C (reflow peak)

equations: Black's equation (electromigration MTTF): MTTF = A · J^(-n) · exp(E_a / (k_B·T)), n ≈ 2 for Al interconnects, E_a ≈ 0.7 eV
Onderdonk fusing equation: I_fuse = S · sqrt(T_melt − T_ambient / (t · ρ_0 · α)) — approximate for short pulses
Joule heating: P = I²·R(T), R(T) = R_0·(1 + α·(T − T_0))
Thermal diffusion (1D): ∂T/∂t = α_D·∂²T/∂x² + q/(ρ·c_p), α_D = k/(ρ·c_p)

sky130_gate_oxide_tddb.note: SKY130 core SOA ceiling; exceeding accelerates TDDB exponentially (E-model: ln(MTTF) ∝ −γ·Vgs, γ ≈ 300 dec/V for 4.1 nm SiO2)

failure_thresholds.aluminium_fusing_note: SKY130 metal (Al) fusing depends on current density; for 1 µm wide met1, typical DC fusing current ≈ 5–10 mA
